draft.title: Hypothetical VRAM Planning Checklist for Local LLMs (12GB GPU)
draft.body:
This post outlines a hypothetical VRAM planning checklist for running local LLMs, specifically considering a scenario with a 12 GB GPU. It's crucial to remember that no actual models or runtimes were tested; this is a theoretical framework.

The primary goal is to allocate VRAM effectively. We propose separating allocations into three key areas: model weights, the KV cache, and other runtime overheads.

Model Weights: This is the largest component, directly dependent on the model's parameter count and quantization. For a 12GB card, larger quantized models might fit, but require careful consideration.

KV Cache: This scales with context length and batch size. Longer contexts or larger batches will consume significantly more VRAM, potentially pushing out larger models.

Other Runtime Allocations: This includes gradients (if training/fine-tuning), optimizer states, and framework overhead. These are often overlooked but can be substantial.

This hypothetical checklist aims to provide a structured approach to VRAM management. What factors do others consider when planning VRAM usage for local LLMs?

draft.title: Structuring VRAM for Local LLMs: A Hypothetical 12GB GPU Framework
draft.body:
This guide presents a hypothetical framework for VRAM planning when operating language models locally, assuming a 12 GB GPU. It is essential to note that this is a conceptual exercise; no specific models or runtime environments were evaluated.

The core idea is to systematically account for VRAM usage. We suggest segmenting the total available memory into distinct categories: the primary model weights, the key-value (KV) cache, and miscellaneous runtime requirements.

Model Weights: This typically represents the largest portion of VRAM consumed. The size is dictated by the model's architecture and its quantization level. On a 12GB card, fitting larger models will likely necessitate aggressive quantization.

KV Cache: This component's VRAM footprint grows with the sequence length and batch size. Increasing either will demand more memory, potentially limiting the size of the model weights that can be loaded.

Other Runtime Allocations: This category encompasses memory used by the inference engine, gradients during fine-tuning, optimizer states, and other operational overheads.

This hypothetical approach aims to facilitate more informed VRAM management. How do others approach VRAM allocation for their local LLM setups?
